slides.headline: Married for love, or for land?
slides.sub: Thomas Gainsborough, Mr and Mrs Andrews, about 1750

slides.headline: Newlyweds
slides.text: Suffolk, around 1750. Robert Andrews and Frances Carter have just married. Young Gainsborough paints them under an oak tree.

slides.headline: Him
slides.text: He stands relaxed, gun under his arm, his dog at his feet. Everything about him says: all of this is my land.

slides.headline: Her
slides.text: She sits stiffly on an elegant bench in a pale blue silk dress. She does not smile, not even a little.

slides.headline: The land
slides.text: Behind them stretch neat fields of wheat, sheep and woods. Their marriage brought two families' estates together.

slides.headline: The empty lap
slides.text: Now look at her lap. It is unfinished, bare canvas. Nobody knows what Gainsborough meant to paint there.

slides.headline: Theories
slides.text: A book? A fan? A baby they hoped for? Some say a bird her husband had shot. No one knows.

slides.headline: The oak
slides.text: The great oak behind them stands for strength and old family roots. Money and love share one bench here.

slides.headline: Love or deal?
slides.text: They look rich, proud and strangely far apart. Do you think this was a love match, or a very good business deal?
